draft.title: Technical and everyday meanings
card: Each subject has its own technical words. These are special words that name ideas in that subject, such as photosynthesis in science.
Some everyday words take on a special meaning in a subject. The word is the same, but the meaning is more exact.
In science, a cell is the smallest living unit of an organism. In maths, volume is the amount of space inside a 3D shape. In maths, a table can be a grid of data.
To choose the right meaning, check which subject you are in and read the words around the term.
draft.remember: The same word can mean different things, so the subject and the nearby words show which meaning is used.

a.q: A student reads: "The volume of the box is 24 cubic centimetres." What does volume mean here?
opts: The amount of space inside the box
How loud the box is when it is dropped
The number of books stored in the box
The pages in one book of a series
a.why: In maths, volume is the amount of space inside a 3D shape, and cubic centimetres measure space. Loudness is the everyday meaning, but it does not fit a measurement of a box.
a.clue: Look at the unit, cubic centimetres.

b.q: In a science lesson, Ravi reads: "Under the microscope, each cell had a clear outer edge." Which meaning of cell fits?
opts: A tiny living unit that makes up an organism
A small room where a prisoner is kept
A phone that is used to make calls
One box in a grid on a page of data
b.why: A microscope is used in science, where a cell is the smallest living unit of an organism. The grid box meaning is tempting because it is also technical, but it belongs to a data table, not a microscope.

a.best: The amount of space inside the box

b.best: A tiny living unit that makes up an organism
